$comment: Single source of truth for the Chart API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: chart
title: Chart
description: Bar, line, area, pie and donut charts drawn in your theme, stacked or smooth, with a legend, tooltips and a data table for screen readers.

label.description: What the chart shows. Names the picture and captions the data table. Required.
label.html: aria-label on svg.vin-chart__svg[role=img] and the table's caption

data.description: One row per category, in order.

index.description: The field that names each category (the x axis).

series.type: { key: string; label?: string; color?: string }[]
series.description: The fields to draw. Pie and donut draw the first one, one slice per row. Colours default to the theme's --vin-chart-1 to --vin-chart-5.

stacked.description: Bar and area: stack the series, so the top is the total.
stacked.html: one bar per category; areas sit on the series below

curve.description: Line and area: smooth draws a monotone curve that never overshoots the data.

centerLabel.description: Donut: caption under the total in the middle. Without it the middle stays empty.

format.description: Formats values in the tooltip and table. Default: 12,400.

tickFormat.description: Formats the y-axis ticks. Default: compact (12K).

indexLabel.description: Heading of the first table column, e.g. "Month".

aspectRatio.description: Width ÷ height of the plot. The chart scales with its container; labels stay full size.

legend.description: Show the legend. Default: when there's more than one series, and always for pie and donut (one key per slice).

theme colours.description: --vin-chart-1 is the accent; 2 to 5 turn its hue around the colour wheel at a readable lightness, so they suit any accent. Override any of them on .vin-chart.

examples.title: Bar
examples.description: Two series side by side. Hover a month, or focus the chart and use the arrow keys, to see its values. In HTML the SVG is static; add data-vin-chart and include vinui.js for the tooltip.

examples.title: Line
examples.description: This week against last week, with a point on each day.

examples.title: Area
examples.description: One series, so no legend. Values and ticks are formatted as rupees.

examples.title: Stacked bar
examples.description: Three series stacked into one bar per month, so the height is the total. The tooltip still lists each series.

examples.title: Stacked area, smooth
examples.description: Desktop and mobile stacked, drawn with a smooth curve.

examples.title: Pie
examples.description: One slice per row. Hover a slice, or focus the chart and use the arrow keys, to see its value.

examples.title: Donut
examples.description: The same data as a donut, with the total and a caption in the middle (centerLabel).

a11y: The SVG has role="img" and a label that says what it shows; the same numbers are in a visually hidden table (caption, column and row headers) right after it.
The legend and axis labels are hidden from screen readers because the table already says it all.
The chart can be focused: Left and Right (or Up and Down), Home and End move between categories and show a tooltip; Escape hides it. The tooltip also follows the pointer.
Series colours start from your accent and keep a mid lightness, so lines and bars stand out on light and dark backgrounds. Colour is never the only cue: the tooltip and table name every series.
Lines keep a 2px stroke at any size, and labels stay full size on small screens because they are HTML, not SVG text.
Pie and donut slices are labelled the same way: the table has one row per slice, and the arrow keys move between slices.
